title: Kugelwald Wooden Marble Run Glungezer Tulfes
name: Kugelwald Wooden Marble Run Glungezer Tulfes
kurzbeschreibung: Kugelwald am Glungezer near Tulfes: the world's largest wooden marble run in a stone pine forest at 1,560 m with spectacular tracks, treehouse, and relaxation areas.
beschreibung:
Overview

The unique Kugelwald am Glungezer is situated at the Halsmarter middle station of the Glungezerbahn cable car high above the Tyrolean Inntal in the municipality of Tulfes (Bezirk Innsbruck-Land) at an altitude of approximately 1,560 metres. Nestled in a centuries-old, wonderfully fragrant high-alpine stone pine forest in the Tuxer Alpen, this multi-award-winning nature and family adventure park covers a wooded area of around 7,000 square metres. As the world's largest outdoor wooden marble run, this natural attraction crafted from Swiss stone pine wood delights children, families, and nature lovers alike.

World's Largest Wooden Marble Run & Nature Experience

The centrepiece of the park is its spectacular marble ball tracks: stretching over hundreds of metres in total length, artfully crafted chutes made of native pine wood wind at various heights through the terrain and between mighty conifers. At the entrance, visitors receive large, hand-turned pine wood balls to send on their journey along the intricate tracks. The balls conquer rapid banked turns, sound stations, jumps, funnels, and track switches. With movable wooden elements, children can even construct their own ball courses. In addition to the tracks, an impressive treehouse, a forest classroom, hammocks for relaxing beneath fragrant pine canopies, and a spacious low-ropes course invite young and old to play, climb, and balance.

Visit & Getting There

Kugelwald am Glungezer is open during the summer operating season of the Glungezerbahn from mid-May to late October, daily from 09:00 to 16:30. Admission to the Kugelwald is free; a wooden pine ball to play on the runs can be purchased at the ticket vending machine for approx. €3.00 and taken home as a fragrant souvenir. Glungezerbahn cable car fare to Halsmarter middle station (2025/2026 season): round trip adults approx. €24.00, children approx. €14.00. Holders of the Innsbruck Card receive discounts. Getting there: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Hall Mitte), continuing on the regional road up to Tulfes to the valley station of the Glungezerbahn (large free car park). By public transport: from Hall in Tirol railway station take bus route 4134 directly to the Glungezerbahn valley station.

Tips

The Halsmarter middle station and the main paths in the Kugelwald are gravel-paved and accessible with all-terrain strollers. Right next to the woodland area, Alpengasthaus Halsmarter features a large sun terrace with a playground and traditional Tyrolean cuisine (outstanding Kaspressknödel!).
